text:
The Darnell Nurse trade is being judged in two cities at once. Edmonton sent him to San Jose on July 1 for Shakir Mukhamadullin and prospect Zack Sharp, and the Sharks took on his full $9.25 million cap hit. This week the Edmonton Journal ran Mike Babcock calling it a "Pretty good deal by Stan," and Pro Hockey Rumors went with "The Darnell Nurse Trade Is A Disaster For The Sharks." Saturday against Utah captured the mix: Max Miller of Sharks Hockey Digest called one Nurse giveaway "a brutal turnover" that put the Mammoth ahead, and Nurse also picked up an assist in the win.

He does the heavy work, over 21 minutes a night with 36 blocked shots and 38 hits in 21 games, but the offense has dried up: three points, one goal on 32 shots. At five on five San Jose has taken 43% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, roughly what it manages without him: not dragging the team down, but not lifting it. Evolving-Hockey's view of last season is kinder than his reputation: replacement level by results, but better by chance quality than his goals showed.
headline: Darnell Nurse carries the weight of a debated trade
